Django News Application
  • Installation

Installation

You can run the application in two ways:

  • Locally with Python and your own MySQL/MariaDB server.

  • With Docker, which starts the app and a MariaDB database together.

Get the project

Clone the repository and open the project folder:

git clone https://github.com/key6308/news-capstone-consolidation.git
cd news-capstone-consolidation

Option A: run locally

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.12

  • A running MySQL or MariaDB server

1. Create a virtual environment and install dependencies

Windows PowerShell:

py -3.12 -m venv .venv          # or: python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

If PowerShell refuses to run Activate.ps1, allow scripts for the current terminal only and try again:

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

macOS / Linux:

python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

2. Create the database

In MySQL or MariaDB, create a database and a user that can access it:

CREATE DATABASE news_capstone CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;
CREATE USER 'news_user'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'choose-a-password';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON news_capstone.* TO 'news_user'@'localhost';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON `test_news_capstone`.* TO 'news_user'@'localhost';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;

The second GRANT lets python manage.py test create and delete its temporary test_news_capstone database.

Note

MariaDB is recommended. MySQL 8 uses caching_sha2_password authentication, which the PyMySQL driver only supports when the cryptography package is installed. With MySQL 8, also run python -m pip install cryptography.

3. Configure environment variables

The settings module reads its configuration from environment variables. The file .env.example lists them all:

Variable

Default

Purpose

DJANGO_SECRET_KEY

dev-only-change-me

Django secret key. Set your own value outside local testing.

DJANGO_DEBUG

True

Debug mode.

ALLOWED_HOSTS

127.0.0.1,localhost

Comma-separated host names the site may be served on.

DB_NAME

news_capstone

Database name.

DB_USER

news_user

Database user.

DB_PASSWORD

change-me

Database password.

DB_HOST / DB_PORT

127.0.0.1 / 3306

Database server address.

APPROVED_API_URL

http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/approved/

Endpoint called when an editor approves an article.

Generate a secret key with the virtual environment active:

python -c "from django.core.management.utils import get_random_secret_key; print(get_random_secret_key())"

Then set the variables in one of these ways.

a) A .env file (recommended). Copy the example file, then edit .env and set DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and DB_PASSWORD. The settings module loads .env from the project root with python-dotenv (installed from requirements.txt). Git ignores .env.

Copy-Item .env.example .env      # Windows PowerShell

cp .env.example .env             # macOS / Linux

b) The terminal. Variables set this way last until the terminal is closed and override values in .env. Windows PowerShell:

$env:DJANGO_SECRET_KEY = "paste-the-generated-key-here"
$env:DB_PASSWORD = "choose-a-password"

macOS / Linux:

export DJANGO_SECRET_KEY="paste-the-generated-key-here"
export DB_PASSWORD="choose-a-password"

Warning

Never commit real passwords, secret keys, or API tokens to the repository.

4. Migrate, test, and run

python manage.py check
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py test
python manage.py runserver

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in a browser. Continue with Quickstart and usage.

The public registration page creates reader and journalist accounts only. To create an editor, run python manage.py createsuperuser, sign in at /admin/, and set the user’s Role to Editor.

Option B: run with Docker

Install Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine with the Compose plugin) and make sure it is running. From the project root:

docker compose up --build

Compose starts a MariaDB container, waits until it is healthy, runs the migrations, and starts Django on http://127.0.0.1:8000/.

To create demo data inside the running container:

docker compose exec web python manage.py seed_demo

Stop the services with Ctrl+C and then:

docker compose down        # keep the database data
docker compose down -v     # also delete the database volume

Note

compose.yaml contains local-development fallback passwords. Set your own DB_PASSWORD, DB_ROOT_PASSWORD, and DJANGO_SECRET_KEY before using it anywhere other than your own computer.
